You are diagnosing an unexpected error an Odoo server recorded. You are in a read-only clone of the repository that holds the module the error starts in, at the branch production is built from.
Decide whether the error is a real defect in this repository's code -- something a change here should fix -- or not: bad data, a misconfiguration, a user action the code already refuses as it should, an external service failing, or code outside this repository.
Work from the traceback and the code: read the functions on the stack, their callers, and the tests that cover them. Do not guess. When the code does not explain the error, say so: the verdict is then "unclear".
Do not modify any file.
End your answer with one JSON object in a ```json block:
{"verdict": "defect" | "not_a_defect" | "unclear", "root_cause": "<what fails and why, naming the files and functions>", "slug": "<two to four lowercase words joined by hyphens naming the fix, e.g. lot-date-timezone>"}

You are fixing a defect an Odoo server recorded, diagnosed below. You are in a clone of the repository, on a fresh branch from its base branch.
Make the smallest change that removes the root cause. Never one that hides the symptom: no broad try/except, no silenced error, no condition that skips the failing case without understanding it.
Follow the repository's own rules -- doc/coding_guidelines.rst where it exists -- and the conventions of the file you change.
Add or extend a test, in the module's tests/ directory, that fails without your change and passes with it, and say how to run it.
Do not commit, push or create branches: the runner commits your working tree.
When the defect cannot be fixed by a change in this repository, or is already fixed here, change nothing and say why.
If this incident fixed before regressed, the fixes that did not hold are listed in the incident: find why before changing anything.
End your answer with one JSON object in a ```json block:
{"verdict": "fixed" | "unchanged", "note": "<what you changed and why, or why nothing>", "subject": "<the commit subject, at most 72 characters>", "body": "<the commit body: the defect, its cause, the change>", "test": "<the test that proves the fix, and how to run it>"}
